content.title: About
content.content: Dried apricots are apricots that have had most of their water removed by sun-drying or dehydration, leaving a chewy, sweet-tart, concentrated fruit. They are eaten as a snack and used in baking, granola, stews, pilafs, and desserts. Some are dried with the pit (in Central Asia, whole dried apricots are called uryuk) and others are halved and pitted.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: It takes several pounds of fresh apricots to make one pound of dried apricots.
Bright orange dried apricots are usually treated with sulfur dioxide, while unsulfured ones are darker brown.
Dried apricots have been a staple food in Central Asia and the Middle East for centuries because they keep for a long time.
Drying concentrates both nutrients and natural sugars.
They are widely used in both sweet and savory dishes, including pilafs and meat stews.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Dried apricots contain beta-carotene, which the body can convert into vitamin A for vision, skin, and immune function.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium supports normal blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Dried apricots contribute fiber that supports digestion.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Dried apricots contain iron, which supports oxygen transport.

items.title: Convenient energy
items.content: Dried apricots are a portable, long-lasting source of quick energy.

items.title: Sulfites
items.content: Sulfured dried apricots can trigger reactions in people with sulfite sensitivity or asthma. Choose unsulfured ones if you are sensitive.

items.title: Concentrated sugar and calories
items.content: Dried apricots are high in natural sugars and calories for their weight, so portions should be small.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Eating a lot of dried apricots may cause bloating or loose stools because of fiber and sorbitol.

items.title: Teeth and potassium
items.content: Sticky dried fruit can cling to teeth, and people with kidney problems or on certain medications should ask a healthcare professional about potassium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried apricots can be eaten as a snack, chopped into oatmeal, yogurt, granola, and salads, or cooked into pilafs, tagines, and stews. They can also be soaked in warm water to soften and used in baking and desserts. Eat a small handful at a time.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dried apricots in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place, where they keep for several months, or in the refrigerator or freezer for longer storage. Keep them away from moisture. Discard dried apricots that show mold or smell fermented.
